findings.reason: a node dispatched to leave "one owner" would leave this identity-based resolution in place, so the plan's stated goal is met only in appearance unless §16 names or excludes this site as it did for `dispatch_sections`.
findings.text: §16 states the repository-to-projects resolution has two spellings and that "Only §10's compares git identity", but `_resolved_node_scope_entries` (reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:904-916) builds its repositories as `repository_identity(root) or Path(root).resolve()` and then reads the same `mounted_repository_projects()` map keyed by that identity (dispatch_claims.py:905-907, consumed by `_scope_derivation_project`'s `repository_projects.get(repository, ())`), so a linked worktree is collapsed onto its main checkout's projects there too; §16 gives an explicit exclusion for the sibling `project_mount_repository` but is silent on this one

rubric_items.done_when: pass — §16's measure names a base-arm control: the new test fails on main because `shadow_source` finds no project for the linked worktree, which matches the code (dispatch.py:205 returns `()` for a worktree path, and the fallback scan finds no `crew.json`).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §16 asserts no gate log of its own; the "new test module" is a source path and no session-scratchpad or node-local temporary path is named.

rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the population claim ("Only §10's compares git identity") omits a third identity-based repository-to-projects site in `reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py`.
